# Master Your Inbox: Summarise and Draft Emails Faster with Apple Intelligence

**By the end of this guide you'll be able to skim a long email in seconds and send a polite, on-point reply without typing the whole thing yourself. This is for anyone who uses Apple Mail on iPhone, iPad or Mac and wants to spend less time drowning in their inbox.**

## Before you start

- **Device you'll need**: An iPhone, iPad or Mac that supports Apple Intelligence. Practically, that means an iPhone 15 Pro or newer, any iPhone 16, an iPad with an M-series chip, or a Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or later). If you're unsure, open Settings and search for "Apple Intelligence".
- **iOS / iPadOS / macOS version**: Update to the latest system update before you start. The Mail features below live inside that update, not in a separate app.
- **Time**: About 5 minutes to set things up, then roughly 30 seconds per email once you're practised.
- **Cost**: Apple Intelligence is free with a supported device, though some features may need you to be signed into iCloud and have a small amount of free iCloud storage available. No extra subscription is required for the Mail tools we cover here.
- **One honest limit**: Apple Intelligence can summarise and draft, but it cannot send email for you. You always review and tap Send yourself — and you should, because the suggestions aren't perfect.

## Step 1 — Turn Apple Intelligence on

Open the **Settings** app on your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Scroll down and tap **Apple Intelligence & Siri** (on Mac it's under **Apple Intelligence** in System Settings). Toggle **Apple Intelligence** to on if it isn't already. A small download starts — you'll see a progress bar labelled "Getting Ready…" and then a message that Apple Intelligence is ready. If you can't see that toggle at all, your device may not support Apple Intelligence; double-check the model list in "Before you start". You'll know it worked when the setting shows a green tick and a short welcome message appears.

## Step 2 — Open Mail and find a long email

Open the **Mail** app from your home screen, Dock or Launchpad. Tap (or click) into your inbox and pick an email with more than a few paragraphs — a newsletter, a meeting recap or a long reply from a colleague works well. The full message opens on screen with the sender at the top and the body below. If your inbox is empty, send yourself a long block of text first, or wait for the next newsletter that lands. You'll know it worked when you can see the full email body and the standard Mail toolbar (Reply, Forward, Archive and so on) at the top or bottom.

## Step 3 — Summarise the email with one tap

At the very top of the open email, look for a small button labelled **Summarise** (it looks like a few stacked lines with sparkle dots ✨). Tap it. A short, plain-English summary slides into view above the original text, usually two or three sentences long. If you don't see the button, scroll to the top of the message — sometimes you have to pull past quoted replies to find it. On some devices the same option sits behind a long-press on the email in your inbox list. You'll know it worked when a neat summary appears and you can still tap "View Original Email" to see the full message again.

💬 Example summary you might see: *"Anna is confirming Tuesday's meeting at 10am, sharing three agenda items, and asking you to review the attached budget before Friday."*

## Step 4 — Start a reply the AI way

Tap **Reply** as you normally would (the curved arrow at the top or bottom of the email). A new compose window opens. Inside that window, look for a small **✨ Apple Intelligence** button or a line that says **"Show Writing Tools"**. Tap it. A small panel appears with options like **Compose**, **Rewrite**, **Make Friendly**, **Make Concise** and **Make Professional**. If you can't see the ✨, look inside the formatting menu (the **Aa** icon above the keyboard on iPhone and iPad, or **Edit → Writing Tools** on Mac). You'll know it worked when a popup or floating bar appears with at least three tone options.

## Step 5 — Tell Apple Intelligence what to write

Tap **Compose** and a small prompt box appears. Type a short instruction in plain English telling the AI what the reply should do — keep it to one sentence. Then tap the arrow or **Send to compose** button. A draft appears in the reply window, written in a neutral, polite tone. If your screen looks different, look for a field labelled **"Ask for anything…"** instead — same idea, different label. If the first draft isn't quite right, edit the prompt or tap **Compose** again for a fresh take.

💬 Example: *"Reply politely, agree to Tuesday 10am, and ask for the budget as a PDF."*

You'll know it worked when a complete draft appears in the reply area with your own original email quoted below it, ready for you to read.

## Step 6 — Polish and send the email yourself

Read the draft out loud once before sending — this is the most important step. If a sentence feels off, tap any paragraph and choose **Rewrite**, **Make Concise** or **Make Professional** from the Writing Tools menu. Add anything personal the AI couldn't know (the recipient's name, a quick joke, a private detail). When you're happy, tap **Send** exactly as you would for any normal email. Apple Intelligence never sends anything on your behalf. You'll know it worked when your message lands in the sent folder and the recipient gets a reply that sounds like you on a calm, well-rested day.

## Common mistakes

- **Mistake: Trusting the summary without checking.** Fix: Always glance at the original email if the summary mentions numbers, dates or money. AI summaries can drop a small but important detail.
- **Mistake: Sending the first draft unchanged.** Fix: Read it once out loud. If it sounds stiff or robotic, tap **Make Friendly** or rewrite your prompt with more direction.
- **Mistake: Looking for a Summarise button on every email.** Fix: The button only shows up on emails long enough to summarise. For a one-line "Thanks!" message, there's nothing to summarise — just reply normally.
- **Mistake: Assuming it works on every device.** Fix: Older iPhones, iPads and Macs don't support Apple Intelligence. If the toggle is missing, the app version may be old, or the device is simply not in the supported list.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** When a school newsletter or community group email lands in your inbox, you can get the gist in two seconds and reply in one tap, instead of saving it for "later" and never getting back to it.
- **For your business or work:** Long client updates, project recaps and meeting notes become three-sentence summaries, so you can triage your inbox in a fraction of the time and reply with a polite, professional draft in seconds.
- **If you're just getting started:** Pick one email you haven't replied to yet and try the Summarise + Compose flow on it today. Treat the AI output as a starting point, not a final answer, and you'll get more comfortable with each reply.

## Try it now

Open Mail, find the longest unread email you have, tap **Summarise**, then tap **Reply → ✨ → Compose** and type: *"Reply warmly, agree to the next step, and ask one clarifying question."* Read the draft, tweak it, and send it. You'll have just triaged and answered an email in under a minute.
